headline: Sterling is about 1.335 dollars on Wednesday morning in Dubai, flat overnight after falling from about 1.344 on Tuesday, when hotter US consumer prices and hawkish words from Fed Governor Waller lifted US yields and the dollar. The US bond market is shut today for Veterans Day, so the next scheduled test is UK growth figures on Thursday morning.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: Futures price a 91.9% chance of a quarter point Fed rise at the meeting ending on 9 December, up from 84% a day earlier, and a 9.1% chance of a half point rise, with better than even odds of a second rise in January, according to Reuters on 11 November. Governor Waller said on 10 November that a half point rise should be considered if October core inflation came in at 0.3% or more, which it did.

drivers.title: US inflation and yields
drivers.text: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected, and 0.3% excluding food and energy against 0.2% expected, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics on 10 November. The US ten year yield rose 13.8 basis points to about 5.00% on the day, according to Reuters, which keeps the dollar supported.

drivers.title: Iran and oil
drivers.text: Brent crude briefly fell below $90 a barrel (about £67) for the first time since August as peace talks continued, according to MUFG on 11 November, and both main oil contracts have lost about 20% this month, according to Euronews on 10 November. President Trump spoke of positive momentum after meeting Qatar's prime minister on 9 November, though Tehran has not confirmed any terms, so the outcome is uncertain.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, its first rise in more than three years, and Governor Bailey said in Zurich on 9 November that the risk of inflation running higher remains a concern. UK growth figures for the third quarter come out on 12 November, forecast at 0.7% for the quarter.

lower: Fed speakers backing a half point rise in December after Tuesday's hotter inflation, which would lift US yields and the dollar once the bond market reopens on Thursday.
Talks with Iran stalling or fresh attacks in the Gulf that send oil back up, which would tend to lift the dollar as a safe haven.
UK growth figures on 12 November below the 0.7% forecast, which would weaken the case for higher UK rates and weigh on the pound.
Bank of England speakers leaning against a further rise in December, which would take away support the pound has.
higher: Fed speakers playing down a half point rise, which would take some strength out of the dollar.
Confirmed progress in the Iran talks that keeps oil falling, which would tend to weaken the dollar.
UK growth figures on 12 November above the 0.7% forecast, which would support the case for higher UK rates and lift the pound.
Softer US producer prices on 13 November than the 0.4% forecast, which would ease pressure for Fed rises and weaken the dollar.
watch: UK growth figures for the third quarter come out on Thursday 12 November at 11:00 Dubai, forecast at 0.7% for the quarter and 0.0% for September alone; stronger figures would support the case for higher UK rates and help someone selling pounds for dirhams, and weaker ones would hurt.

feed.title: Sterling has edged lower as the dollar firms again in the European morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3349 at 09:25 Dubai to about 1.3331 by 10:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1165 to 1.1153, so most of the move came from a slightly firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a fresh trigger: FXStreet described the dollar index as steady near 102.20 in Asian trade, with futures still pricing about a 91% chance of a December Fed rise after Tuesday's hotter US prices and Chicago Fed President Goolsbee calling them borderline disturbing. A firmer Fed outlook keeps the dollar supported, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and no UK figures are due until Thursday.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as the dollar keeps its gains
feed.text: Asian trading brought no fresh news for the pound or the dollar: Reuters reported the dollar index steady at 102.22, near its highest since 28 October, after Tuesday's 0.5% rise on hotter US prices, with futures now pricing a 91.9% chance of a quarter point Fed rise in December. The US bond market is shut today for Veterans Day, and no US or UK figures are due until Thursday. GBP/USD stayed between about 1.3342 and 1.3352 from midnight to 07:30 Dubai and stood near 1.3346 at 07:30 Dubai, close to where it ended in New York.

feed.title: Sterling has recovered a little as the dollar eases in late New York trade
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3322 at 21:40 Dubai to about 1.3340 by 22:45 Dubai, after a step from about 1.3334 to 1.3340 between 22:35 and 22:40 Dubai, and stood near 1.3342 at 23:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1144 to 1.1160, so the gain came from a slightly softer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a trigger: the US ten year auction at 22:00 Dubai was described as soft, at a yield of 5.02% with dealers left holding 10%, and Treasury yields stayed near the day's highs, which would normally support the dollar rather than weaken it. The move looks like some of the day's dollar gains after hotter US prices being given back, with a December Fed rise still almost fully priced.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped again as the dollar holds its gains after US prices
feed.text: The dollar kept its footing into the evening after October's hotter US consumer prices and Fed Governor Waller's call for a December rise, with CNBC reporting the CME FedWatch tool at about 88% for a quarter point rise in December and 11% for a half point rise, and the US two year yield up about 0.12 points on the day at about 4.68%, according to ActionForex. Higher US yields and a firmer Fed mean a stronger dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3350 at 19:40 Dubai to a low near 1.3309 at 20:40 Dubai and stood near 1.3322 at 21:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell from about 1.1164 to 1.1140, so most of the move came from the dollar; no fresh news was found to explain this particular step, and it looks like a continuation of the day's move.

feed.title: Sterling has slid further as the dollar extends its gains after US prices
feed.text: The dollar kept rising through the afternoon after hotter US inflation and Fed Governor Waller's call for a December rise, with FXStreet reporting the CME FedWatch tool at about 85% for a quarter point Fed rise in December and 14% for a half point rise; a firmer Fed means higher US yields and a stronger dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD eased from about 1.3392 at 17:39 Dubai to about 1.3370 by 19:00 Dubai, then dropped from about 1.3372 at 19:22 Dubai to about 1.3350 by 19:37 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell only from about 1.1186 to 1.1167 over the whole period, so the pound did a little worse than the euro. No report read names a trigger for the sharp step after 19:20 Dubai, and nothing new about the UK economy or the Bank of England has been found to explain the pound's extra weakness.

feed.title: The dollar has jumped after hotter US inflation figures
feed.text: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected, and 0.3% excluding food and energy against 0.2% expected, with energy up 0.7%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Hotter US inflation makes a December Fed rise more likely and, with Governor Waller saying a core figure around 0.3% could justify a half point rise, lifts US yields and the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3421 just before the release to about 1.3392 within a minute and stood near 1.3393 eight minutes later, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1209 to 1.1183, so the move came from a stronger dollar.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed as Fed Governor Waller calls for a December rise
feed.text: Speaking in London at 13:00 Dubai, Fed Governor Waller said US inflation is too high and that he would support a quarter point rise in December even if October prices improve, with a half point rise possibly needed if core inflation comes in around 0.3% or higher, according to FXStreet and CNBC. A firmer Fed means higher US yields and a stronger dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3452 just before he began to about 1.3434 within two minutes and to about 1.3429 by 13:10 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1248 to 1.1227, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound.

feed.title: The dollar has eased at the European open ahead of US prices
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3444 at 10:55 Dubai to about 1.3455 by 11:35 Dubai and stood near 1.3454 at 12:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1222 to 1.1241, so the gain came from a slightly softer dollar rather than news about the pound. FXStreet reported Brent crude down more than 20% over the past week at fresh two-month lows on progress in Middle East diplomacy, and Brown Brothers Harriman said the dollar had pared some of Friday's jobs gains; cheaper oil and calmer Gulf tension tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. No single fresh trigger is named for this step, and traders are waiting for Fed Governor Waller at 13:00 Dubai and US consumer prices at 17:30 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has weakened on reports that US and Iran talks have revived
feed.text: Late on Monday, Al Arabiya reported, citing unnamed sources, that a proposal from Qatar and Pakistan had revived serious talks between the US and Iran, including a limit of 3.67% on Iranian uranium enrichment; neither government has confirmed the terms, and US crude fell nearly 4.5% on the day to $86.37 a barrel (about £64), according to FXStreet. Calmer Gulf tension and cheaper oil tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3425 at 23:35 Dubai to about 1.3438 by 23:42 Dubai and touched 1.3451 just before midnight, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1204 to 1.1220, and the pair has held near 1.3440 through the quiet Asian morning.

feed.title: The Bank of England Governor has begun his Zurich talk with little effect so far
feed.text: Andrew Bailey began his lecture at the University of Zurich at 21:25 Dubai, a few days after the Bank raised its rate by a quarter point to 4.00%, its first rise in more than three years; the event is billed as opening remarks followed by discussion, and no report read so far carries anything new he has said on rates. GBP/USD barely moved, standing near 1.3420 just before he began and near 1.3420 at 21:38 Dubai, after a small rise from about 1.3414 to 1.3421 in the ten minutes beforehand that EUR/USD matched, so that step came from a slightly softer dollar. A firm line on further rises would tend to lift the pound and more dirhams per pound would follow, while a cautious one would tend to weigh on it.

feed.title: The dollar has slipped again after the London close
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3396 at 20:04 Dubai to about 1.3412 by 20:19 Dubai and settled near 1.3409, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1190 to 1.1201, so the gain came from a softer dollar rather than news about the pound. FXStreet put the dollar index at about 101.85, down 0.44% on the day, with US crude more than 3% lower at about $86.85 a barrel (about £65) as President Trump played down the chance of new strikes on Iran; cheaper oil and calmer Gulf tension tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. No report read names a fresh trigger for this step itself: it began just after the 4pm London benchmark rates were set, and a New York Fed survey at 20:12 Dubai showed inflation expectations unchanged at 3% for one year ahead.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped back below 1.34 in the London afternoon
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3415 at 18:15 Dubai to a low of about 1.3397 at 19:30 Dubai and stood near 1.3399 at 19:40 Dubai, while EUR/USD held near 1.1192, so the fall came from a slightly softer pound rather than a stronger dollar. No report read names a cause for it; traders are waiting for the Bank of England Governor in Zurich at 21:25 Dubai, where a firm tone on rates would tend to lift the pound and a cautious one would tend to weigh on it, and for US consumer prices on Tuesday.

feed.title: The pound has held its gains in a quiet London morning
feed.text: GBP/USD has moved in a narrow band since the last update, from 1.3410 at 12:39 Dubai to a low of about 1.3403 near 13:15 Dubai and a high of about 1.3426 near 13:50 Dubai, and stood near 1.3416 at 15:40 Dubai. EUR/USD drifted up in step, from about 1.1183 to about 1.1192, so the small gain came from a slightly softer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reported the dollar index holding just above 102.00 in European trading after Friday's jobs rally, with oil lower on the Iran talks; no report read names a fresh cause for the moves since, and traders are waiting for the Bank of England Governor in Zurich this evening and US consumer prices on Tuesday.

feed.title: The dollar has fallen further at the London open as oil slides
feed.text: Brent crude fell nearly 2% to $96.39 a barrel (about £72) on Monday morning on hopes of a deal between the US and Iran, according to Investing.com, after President Trump said new strikes were highly unlikely while talks progressed, though Secretary of State Rubio said there had been no progress. Cheaper oil and calmer Gulf tension tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD rose from about 1.3387 at 12:00 Dubai to about 1.3410 by 12:35 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1168 to 1.1185, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound.

feed.title: The dollar has kept edging lower through the Dubai morning
feed.text: GBP/USD climbed steadily from about 1.3365 at 08:00 Dubai to about 1.3382 by 10:38 Dubai, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1150 to 1.1160, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reported at 08:14 Dubai that the dollar index had slipped to around 102.20 after two days of gains, as lower oil prices eased inflation worries following President Trump's remark that new strikes on Iran were highly unlikely while talks continued; no report read names a fresh cause for the later rise. A softer dollar means more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as Trump plays down new strikes on Iran
feed.text: In a CNN interview on Sunday, President Trump said new US strikes on Iran were highly unlikely as long as talks progressed, and Brent crude fell 0.75% to $97.58 a barrel (about £73) in early Asian trading, according to Investing.com, even after a Houthi missile attack caused limited damage to Saudi Aramco's offices in Riyadh. Calmer Gulf tension and cheaper oil tend to weaken the dollar, which means more dirhams per pound. GBP/USD reopened near 1.3329 at 02:00 Dubai on Monday, a little below Friday's close of about 1.3349, then rose to about 1.3368 by 06:00 Dubai, with EUR/USD rising in step from about 1.1128 to 1.1151, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again late in New York trading
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3369 at 21:38 Dubai to about 1.3350 by 21:53 Dubai and stood near 1.3353 at 22:36 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1150 to about 1.1139, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reports the dollar index near 102.15 at 22:01 Dubai, up from a five week low near 101.24 earlier in the week, with traders pricing an 80% chance of a Fed rise in December after the strong jobs figures. No report read names a cause for this particular fall, and none reports what Fed Governor Bowman said at 21:15 Dubai; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: The dollar has eased as US shares rebound at the open
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3346 at 18:30 Dubai to about 1.3365 by 18:37 Dubai, as Wall Street opened, and EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1129 to 1.1143, so the move came from a softer dollar rather than from news about the pound. Yahoo Finance reports the Nasdaq up 1.7% and Treasury yields pulling back from their highs after the jobs figures; no report read names a direct cause for the currency move, but a calmer stock market tends to reduce demand for the dollar as a safe haven, which means more dirhams per pound.

feed.title: US consumer mood has improved and inflation fears have eased
feed.text: The University of Michigan's early November survey of consumer sentiment rose to 51.0 against a forecast of about 48.1, and households' expectations for inflation a year ahead fell to 4.3% from 4.7%, with five year expectations at 3.4% from 3.5%. Firmer sentiment usually helps the dollar, but lower inflation expectations ease pressure on the Fed to raise rates. GBP/USD dipped from 1.3361 to 1.3355 in the first two minutes, then climbed to about 1.3375 by 19:24 Dubai and stood near 1.3368 at 19:38 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has strengthened after strong US jobs figures
feed.text: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against about 65,000 expected, unemployment fell to 4.1% against 4.2% expected, and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% in the month against 0.3% expected, with August and September revised up by a combined 84,000, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. A firmer job market makes a Fed rise in December more likely: Reuters reports bets on a rise up from 70% to 78%, the two year Treasury yield up 5 basis points to 4.52% and the dollar index up 0.7%. GBP/USD fell from 1.3387 to a low of 1.3363 within a minute of the release, recovered to about 1.3383 by 17:34 Dubai, then slid to about 1.3343 by 18:24 Dubai as EUR/USD fell in step, before edging back to about 1.3361; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped again as share markets fall worldwide
feed.text: GBP/USD edged up from about 1.3401 at 11:40 Dubai to 1.3406 at 12:15 Dubai, then fell to about 1.3383 by 13:35 Dubai; EUR/USD rose and fell in step, from about 1.1170 to 1.1184 and back to 1.1166, so the move came mainly from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. NBC News reports London's FTSE 100 down 1.6% at the open after heavy falls in Asia, with South Korea's Kospi down more than 8%, as worries over artificial intelligence companies after the Democratic sweep of Congress spread, and MUFG, quoted by FXStreet, says the dollar is drawing safe haven demand as AI shares slide. No report read names a cause for the precise timing of the fall, and a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has fallen as investors turn to the dollar for safety
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3424 at 09:40 Dubai to a low of 1.3393 at 11:34 Dubai, with sharp drops at 11:02 and 11:28, and stood near 1.3397 at 11:38 Dubai; EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1194 to 1.1166, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FXStreet reports the dollar edging up in early European trade on demand for safety after Thursday's sell off in US shares, which Reuters links to the Democratic sweep of Congress and fears of tighter scrutiny of artificial intelligence companies, with the Nasdaq having its deepest one day fall since April 2025. No report read names a cause for the two sharp drops themselves, and a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped overnight as the dollar firms before the jobs figures
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3459 at 03:15 Dubai to about 1.3432 by 07:35 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1220 to about 1.1198, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. FX.co reports the dollar index rising to about 101.7 in Asian trade as investors position for the US jobs figures due at 17:30 Dubai; no other news read names a cause. A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped late in New York as the dollar firms
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3484 at 22:00 Dubai to about 1.3447 by 23:38 Dubai, and EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1236 to about 1.1212, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from news about the pound. No report read names a cause; it came on a day when US shares fell sharply on a sell off in technology and chip companies, with the Nasdaq down about 4% in the morning, and a nervous stock market tends to draw money into the dollar. FXStreet reports the dollar index revisiting about 101.70 as traders wait for Friday's US jobs figures.
